title: PHOTOVOLTAIK
description: Photovoltaik (photovoltaics) is a renewable electricity generation technology and the core technology for decentralized power generation in Austria, identified as a key and essential pillar for the country’s electricity supply, decarbonization goals, and the achievement of energy and climate neutrality targets. Photovoltaics is central to Austria’s energy transformation and energy transition, with increasing shares in electricity supply and a pivotal role in achieving national and EU climate objectives. The technology is the main focus of expansion targets, regulatory measures, quality assurance, and market support, with current and future deployment metrics and policy targets discussed for Austria. Photovoltaics is referenced throughout relevant documents as a major component in renewable energy generation, grid integration, and strategic energy objectives for Austria.

title: ÖSTERREICH
description: Austria (ÖSTERREICH) is the national geographic and jurisdictional scope for all described laws, strategies, policies, regulations, metrics, targets, infrastructure, market measures, and cooperative actions concerning photovoltaic (PV) development, PV expansion, energy communities, digitalization, energy policy, research, renewable energy objectives, market participation, innovation, production, education measures, economic value creation, energy market, solar industry participation, reported PV market metrics, deployment potential, sectoral impacts, and energy and climate targets, including acceptance of PV installations, energy system transformation, increased energy sovereignty, and economic effects; Austria is the primary focus for the solar market and clean technology strategies at both national and European levels referenced throughout the source text.

title: ÖSTERREICHISCHE PHOTOVOLTAIK-STRATEGIE
description: The "ÖSTERREICHISCHE PHOTOVOLTAIK-STRATEGIE" (Austrian Photovoltaic Strategy) is a strategy policy for Austria that provides a framework for the expansion, market development, innovation, and social acceptance of photovoltaic (PV) technologies. It outlines framework conditions, targets, objectives, vision, measures, and strategic action fields for coordinated national PV expansion, and includes guidelines and directives for the optimal planning and support of technical, economic, regulatory, and social aspects of PV expansion. The strategy is described as a detailed planning document and a "living" document, intended to be adapted to changing developments, and is relevant to supporting national research, workforce development, and sector-wide strategic PV expansion up to 2040. Its implementation status is described as in force or ongoing in some sources, and as planned/issued or unknown in others.

title: PV-ANLAGE
description: PV-ANLAGE (photovoltaic system) refers to a technology for producing electricity from solar energy, encompassing individual and collective installations on buildings, fields, or infrastructure, and is referenced in contexts such as Austrian solar-market development, studies, installation guidance, and building integration. PV-ANLAGE may include installations with storage and energy-management systems, require grid access, and be subject to approval and quality measures, as well as technical, ecological, and planning considerations.

title: PHOTOVOLTAIK-STRATEGIE
description: Policy type: strategy; Jurisdiction: Austria; Status: present in this document; Source meaning: the strategy defines action areas and measures needed for successful Austrian PV-market transformation and achievement of energy and climate targets.

title: PHOTOVOLTAIK (PV)
description: Photovoltaics (PV) is a solar energy technology explicitly mentioned as central to Austria’s domestic solar market and value creation, and is referenced as a focus of acceptance, technical, ecological, and economic measures in Austria.

title: FOTOVOLTAIKANLAGE
description: A photovoltaic installation/system used for generating electricity from sunlight, central to the regulatory and support schemes discussed.

title: ELEKTRIZITÄTSWIRTSCHAFTSGESETZ (ELWG)
description: The ELEKTRIZITÄTSWIRTSCHAFTSGESETZ (ElWG), or Electricity Industry Act, is a law in Austria that, as of early 2024, is in legislative review and described as new or updated. The Act aims to modernize Austria’s electricity market regulatory framework by introducing measures such as increased transparency in the grid, digitalization of distribution networks, establishment of new market roles, and incentives for faster integration of renewable energy installations. It also addresses issues related to the connection and operation of renewable-energy plants, especially photovoltaics, and mandates regular net development plans at the distribution level. The status is described variously as in legislative review, new/updated, or proposed/adopted (not precisely specified in the supplied descriptions).

title: ENERGIEGEMEINSCHAFTEN
description: ENERGIEGEMEINSCHAFTEN refers to energy communities in Austria through which residents participate in shared photovoltaic (PV) generation and electricity use; these communities represent a new market model in Austria, enabling joint participation in electricity generation and use, are supported through new legal and policy frameworks and by dedicated organizations, and are referenced as operators of shared PV and district storage facilities as well as intended users of emergency and backup power systems.

title: ERNEUERBAREN-AUSBAU-GESETZ (EAG)
description: The Erneuerbaren-Ausbau-Gesetz (EAG), also known as the Renewable Expansion Act, is a law in force in Austria that serves as the legislative basis for renewable-energy expansion in the country. The EAG introduces a fundamentally modernised and market-oriented support system for renewable electricity installations, aiming to establish a long-term stable investment climate. It sets the framework for photovoltaic (PV) expansion, including provisions such as the market premium (Marktprämie) as a major financial support measure for PV deployment and investment grants for Agri-PV under certain agricultural-use conditions. The EAG also sets Austria's nationally balanced renewable electricity target for 2030.

title: BEVÖLKERUNG
description: BEVÖLKERUNG refers to the Austrian general public or general population, whose acceptance, participation, and benefit are considered central to strategy objectives and the successful integration of PV (photovoltaic) systems, particularly on buildings, parking lots, and construction facilities.

title: STROMNETZ
description: The electricity grid (Stromnetz) is the infrastructure to which PV installations are to be connected, described as fundamental for secure renewable energy supply and stable networks, and identified as enabling the integration and distribution of large shares of PV-generated electricity. The supplied descriptions note that the Stromnetz is being incorporated with digitalization and data exchange capabilities and faces challenges from increased renewables, market coupling, and electrification, with calls for simplified and less bureaucratic access.

title: PHOTOVOLTAIKANLAGEN
description: PHOTOVOLTAIKANLAGEN refers to photovoltaic installations or PV systems in Austria, which are concrete installations designed for operation over more than 25 years and whose deployment targets both private individuals and companies, including installations with orientations optimized for edge times (Randzeiten) or winter periods.

title: PHOTOVOLTAIK-ERZEUGUNGSSPITZEN
description: Constraint type: technical; Geographic scope: Austria; Source meaning: Peaks in PV generation can no longer be fully absorbed by the public electricity grid.

title: INTEGRIERTER ÖSTERREICHISCHER NETZINFRASTRUKTURPLAN (NIP)
description: The INTEGRIERTER ÖSTERREICHISCHER NETZINFRASTRUKTURPLAN (NIP), or Integrated Austrian Network Infrastructure Plan, is a strategic infrastructure plan for Austria that provides a framework for the integrated development of transmission network infrastructure for electricity and gas to support the transition to a climate-neutral energy system. The NIP outlines area potentials for photovoltaic (PV) installation on buildings, infrastructures, and open areas, with regular updates and alignment with demand estimates. Its potential assessments also serve as a basis for figures and scenarios used in the Photovoltaic Strategy. The policy is described as ongoing/adopted, in force/implemented (implied as existing in the text), with the specific implementation status stated as ongoing/adopted or in force/implemented, and the status is noted as unknown in one description. The jurisdiction is Austria.

title: QUALIFIZIERTE FACHKRÄFTE
description: Qualified skilled workers needed for the expansion and operation of the photovoltaic sector in Austria, whose securing is an explicit policy and training goal.

title: KLIMA- UND ENERGIEFONDS
description: The KLIMA- UND ENERGIEFONDS (Climate and Energy Fund) is an Austrian organization responsible for supporting energy communities and innovation in the solar sector through targeted funding initiatives, including programmes for storage initiatives and flagship photovoltaic (PV) projects. It commissions studies and market analysis for PV deployment, is referenced as a co-provider of PV expansion funding in 2023 under the EAG, and was responsible for launching the subsidy programme for large storage in 2023.

title: E-CONTROL
description: E-CONTROL, also referred to as E-Control, is the Austrian energy regulatory authority identified as the publisher or responsible party for the Aktionsplan Netzanschluss (July 2023), as well as for studies on flexibility, action plans for grid connection, and contributions to network development and system integration. E-Control is named as a key actor necessary for implementing photovoltaic (PV) expansion measures, planning and operating the electricity grid, and fulfilling other relevant roles in the Austrian PV transformation, particularly regarding grid connection and operation of renewable installations.

title: AGRI-PV-ANLAGE
description: AGRI-PV-ANLAGE refers to a form of photovoltaic installation integrated into agriculture that enables dual use of agricultural land for both farming and electricity production, allowing continued predominant agricultural activity on the same area. This type of photovoltaic system is referenced for its potential contributions to acceptance, biodiversity, enhanced land-use efficiency, and providing new income opportunities for agriculture.

title: MADE IN EUROPE-BONUS
description: The “Made in Europe-Bonus” is a national Austrian measure that offers a subsidy premium of up to 20% of the funding level for PV projects using components produced in Europe.

title: HEIMISCHE PV-WIRTSCHAFT
description: Policy type: strategy/action field; Jurisdiction: Austria; Status: outlined as an action area in the PV strategy; Source meaning: The domestic PV industry is the focus of a defined action area to secure value creation and economic opportunity.

title: BMK-AUSBILDUNGSINITIATIVE „JUST TRANSITION“
description: Training initiative by Austria’s BMK focusing on education and upskilling in photovoltaics, electrotechnology/installation, and roofing to provide necessary competencies for the energy transition.

title: PV-TECHNOLOGIEN
description: Photovoltaic technologies, including new and improved PV solutions and components, targeted by research, innovation, and industrial support measures.

description: Target: PV expansion potential; Target value: 41; Unit: TWh; Deadline: 2040; Geographic scope: Austria; Status: scenario; Source meaning: The Integrated Austrian Network Infrastructure Plan (ÖNIP/NIP) identifies a technical deployment potential of 41 TWh PV electricity generation by 2040.

title: ENERGIEWENDE
description: Policy type: broad transition process; Jurisdiction: Austria; Status: ongoing; Source meaning: The energy transition refers to the fundamental transformation of Austria's energy system, in which the expansion of photovoltaics plays a central and cross-sectoral role.

title: BUNDESMINISTERIUM FÜR KLIMASCHUTZ, UMWELT, ENERGIE, MOBILITÄT, INNOVATION UND TECHNOLOGIE (BMK)
description: The BUNDESMINISTERIUM FÜR KLIMASCHUTZ, UMWELT, ENERGIE, MOBILITÄT, INNOVATION UND TECHNOLOGIE (BMK), also known in English as the Austrian Federal Ministry for Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation and Technology, is responsible for climate, environmental, and energy policy, and is referenced as the publisher or commissioner of several policy documents and statistical market reports, including serving as the publisher and initiator of the Austrian Photovoltaic Strategy.

title: ENERGIEGEMEINSCHAFTEN (EGS)
description: Energy Communities (EGs) are collective models in Austria enabling joint photovoltaic expansion, shared production and use of renewable energy, and participation in energy markets.

title: UMWELTFÖRDERUNGSGESETZ (UFG)
description: Policy type: law; Jurisdiction: Austria; Status: in force; Source meaning: Federal Environmental Support Act covers promotion of water management, environmental measures, contaminated site remediation, biodiversity, and climate protection measures in Austria.

title: GEBÄUDEINTEGRIERTE PV
description: Building-integrated PV including showcase and flagship projects implemented across Austria, referenced for mobilizing sealed surfaces.

title: EUROPÄISCHE UNION (EU)
description: The European Union (EU), referred to as EUROPÄISCHE UNION (EU), acts as the jurisdiction for overarching renewable energy targets and requirements implemented in Austria, serves as the collective jurisdiction for referenced EU-level industrial, research, and regulatory initiatives related to photovoltaics, solar manufacturing, funding, and value chain resilience, and is the jurisdiction referenced in connection with the Net Zero Industry Act, the EU Taxonomy, and cross-border solar production initiatives.
